question_text: The meristem found at the tips of roots and shoots is the:
explanation: Apical meristems produce the primary tissues and increase the length of the plant.
subject: Biology

question_text: The meristem that helps grasses regenerate after grazing is the:
explanation: Intercalary meristems lie between mature tissues at the base of internodes and leaves.
subject: Biology

question_text: The cork cambium is a:
explanation: Vascular cambium and cork cambium are lateral meristems that cause growth in girth.
subject: Biology

question_text: Thin-walled, living, isodiametric cells that store food belong to:
explanation: Parenchyma forms the basic ground tissue and is concerned with photosynthesis, storage and secretion.
subject: Biology

question_text: In collenchyma the corners of the cells are thickened with:
explanation: This thickening gives flexible mechanical support to young stems and petioles.
subject: Biology

question_text: At maturity the cells of sclerenchyma are typically:
explanation: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity.
subject: Biology

question_text: The gritty texture of guava pulp is due to:
explanation: Sclereids are short, dead cells with narrow lumens and are found in fruit walls and seed coats.
subject: Biology

question_text: Vessels are generally absent in the xylem of:
explanation: Gymnosperm xylem has tracheids and lacks vessels (except Gnetales).
subject: Biology

question_text: Protoxylem lies toward the periphery (exarch condition) in:
explanation: Roots are exarch, while stems are endarch with protoxylem toward the pith.
subject: Biology

question_text: Companion cells are closely associated with:
explanation: Companion cells help sieve tube elements load and unload sugars.
subject: Biology

question_text: Companion cells are absent in the phloem of:
explanation: Gymnosperms have albuminous cells with sieve cells instead.
subject: Biology

question_text: The only living element of the xylem is:
explanation: Xylem parenchyma stores food and conducts water radially.
subject: Biology

question_text: Dumb-bell shaped guard cells are characteristic of:
explanation: Grasses have dumb-bell shaped guard cells; dicots have kidney-shaped ones.
subject: Biology

question_text: Root hairs are:
explanation: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells that absorb water and minerals.
subject: Biology

question_text: Vascular bundles are open, with cambium between xylem and phloem, in:
explanation: Open bundles allow secondary growth in dicot stems; monocot bundles are closed.
subject: Biology

question_text: Scattered, closed vascular bundles are seen in:
explanation: Monocot stems have closed bundles scattered in the ground tissue.
subject: Biology

question_text: Xylem and phloem lie on different radii (radial arrangement) in:
explanation: Roots have radial bundles; stems and leaves have conjoint bundles.
subject: Biology

question_text: The hypodermis of a dicot stem is:
explanation: The hypodermis is collenchymatous in dicot stems and sclerenchymatous in monocot stems.
subject: Biology

question_text: Pith is small or inconspicuous in:
explanation: Monocot roots have a large well-developed pith, whereas dicot roots have a small pith or none.
subject: Biology

question_text: Lateral roots arise from the:
explanation: Pericycle cells divide to form lateral roots and also contribute to the cambium in dicot roots.
subject: Biology

question_text: Casparian strips are found in the:
explanation: They are suberin deposits on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells.
subject: Biology

question_text: In a dorsiventral leaf the palisade parenchyma lies toward the:
explanation: Palisade cells are elongated and lie below the upper (adaxial) epidermis, and spongy cells lie toward the lower surface.
subject: Biology

question_text: An isobilateral leaf is typical of:
explanation: Monocot leaves have stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll.
subject: Biology

question_text: Bulliform cells help in:

options.A: rolling of leaves in grasses to reduce water loss

explanation: These large empty colourless cells on the upper epidermis of grass leaves lose water and cause the leaf to curl inward.
subject: Biology

question_text: The vascular cambium produces:
explanation: Secondary xylem is added toward the pith and secondary phloem toward the periphery.
subject: Biology

question_text: Compared with autumn wood, spring wood:

options.A: has narrow vessels and is dark
options.B: has wider vessels and is lighter

explanation: Spring wood is lighter with wider xylem elements; autumn wood is darker and denser.
subject: Biology

question_text: Heartwood:

options.B: contains tannins and resins and does not conduct water
options.C: is the outermost layer of wood

explanation: Heartwood is dark and dead, resistant to microbes, and gives mechanical support.
subject: Biology

question_text: Phelloderm is the:
explanation: Phellogen cuts off phellem (cork) outward and phelloderm (secondary cortex) inward.
subject: Biology

question_text: Lenticels help in:
explanation: Lenticels are lens-shaped openings in the bark that allow gas exchange.
subject: Biology

question_text: Monocot stems usually lack secondary growth because their vascular bundles:
explanation: Closed bundles lack cambium, so there is no cambial activity.
subject: Biology
